input.summary: parts/shell.mjs (P1 Massing and shell) is unchanged: it wrote 1177 cells with 0 refused, and make.sh produced build.nbt. The only P1 report is OFF-PALETTE polished_blackstone_brick_stairs x64, which comes from roof.json (eave "polished_blackstone_brick", roof laid right after P1), not from shell.mjs.
left: OFF-PALETTE polished_blackstone_brick_stairs x64 is still in the build. Source: roof.json line 5, "eave": "polished_blackstone_brick". polished_blackstone_brick_stairs is a real block but not in palette.json (roof_eave lists only spruce_stairs and spruce_slab). Fix belongs to the roof owner, not shell.mjs: point roof.json's eave at a palette block (e.g. spruce_stairs/spruce_slab, or deepslate_tile/cobbled_deepslate if the eave should read as stone), or add the block to palette.json's roof_eave role if the design wants it. I did not edit roof.json or palette.json, since they are outside the file I was asked to fix.

parts-report.json attributes this OFF-PALETTE line to P1 (because the roof is laid right after the shell), while make.sh's stdout prints it on the roof line. Expect it to keep showing under P1 in the report until roof.json changes.

Not P1's, for the owners: P6 sides REFUSED (19,7,13) spruce_trapdoor wanted, white_wool already there (the wing gable vent cell is daub from P1 at shell.mjs:75, so P6 must not write it or P1 must leave it unset); room 3 bakehouse REFUSED (18,2,21) smoker wanted, smoker already there (P3 or the room already placed it).

waste.what: Traced the OFF-PALETTE line to its real source by reading parts-report.json, roof.json and palette.json by hand, and confirmed block names one by one with mcd blocks --check.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls; no edits made
waste.tool: A make.sh/runParts report that names the file and key that produced an off-palette block (e.g. roof.json:5 eave=polished_blackstone_brick) and attributes it to the roof rather than the part before it. A palette pre-check on roof.json and every spec file would also have caught it before the parts ran.
